When someone orders a Martini from you as a bartender, theres 3 questions you should ask:

  1. Gin or Vodka?
  2. How dry?
  3. Olive or twist?

If they want gin, and don't name a brand pick a strong juniper one with a high abv/proof, the coldness of the drink subdues the flavour, you want that flavour. The stronger the gin, the colder the Martini.

If they want it: extra dry: pour vermouth in mixing glass, rinse, pour out. Dry pour vermouth over ice, quick stir to cover ice, pour out. Wet/Not too dry 1 part vermouth to 4 Parts gin.You can use more precise measures if you wish, but these above suffice IMHO

Olive or Lemon twist is pretty much what it says on the tin. A lemon twist is more traditional, especially with gin and it makes more sense, Olive is the usual option for vodka. But it can be interchanged. Just don't put any blue cheese stuffed shit in there (why would you add an oily garnish with fat floating in your drink to the most refreshing drink known to man? WHY?)

If a patron does not have the answers to these questions they don't have a preference or they don't know so don't bombard them with questions, just make the best damn gin martini (with a twist) you can, and like. It will become their regular way of drinking it.

Don't ask if they want it shaken or stirred, you look like an imbecile when you do, Its like the chef asking me if I want my eggs cooked on a low heat or high heat. I'ts stirred. If they wanted it shaken they would have said so from the start and then you make it the way they want of course. But please god never ask, I swear I change my order to a beer if the bartender asks me this.

(BTW a martini is stirred because it gives you more control over the temperature and rate of dilution, you only shake when the ingredients are hard to mix like with juice/eggs/cream etc but that is a topic for a different day)

Same with "dirty". No need to ask, a dirty martini is a different cocktail all together, they would have ordered it from the beginning if they wanted it.

Finally, look after your vermouth, it's like wine. keep it in the fridge and buy something good use it within a week, 2 weeks if you push it. If you can't move it fast enough then don't have more than 1 brand in your bar.

Use a cold mixing glass, and ice up your cocktail glass with ice and soda while you prepare the drink. Stir that thing till its fucking cold, you will know when.

How do I like mine?

  1. Gin - Tanqueray

  3. Twist

Cold as is humanly possible.

TLDR: Easy drink. Get it right.

It is a debate that can range on forever. I do not care much for the god damned blasphemy side of things but I simply do not see the point in shaking a martini.

  • It does not make the drink colder.
  • It does not mix it better.
  • It's not quicker.

What it does do: * It dilutes the drink (which is good, but I'd rather have more control over how much I dilute it by) * It increases the volume. (your bar manager might like that) * It makes it cloudy (some people like that) * It makes the drinker feel like James bond (idiots like that)

Again, if a guest asks me I will do it, no questions asked, and I 100% understand where they come from. But with a fellow bartender I will argue this tooth and nail.
